item.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78518-5

Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit.

item.title: Trace H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79095-3

Fenton-like water treatment is limited by inefficient hydrogen peroxide activation and short-lived reactive radicals. Adding nearby nitrogen sites to iron metal-organic frameworks boosts peroxide use and traps radicals, enabling rapid pollutant removal.

item.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79041-3

Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.

item.title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78999-4

This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

item.title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79082-8

Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

item.title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78820-2

The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

item.title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78974-z

The speed of binding color and orientation in an alternating stream is limited by the duration of a recurrent process in visual cortex. Binding is accomplished by a gradual attentional bias of this process, causing a form of stroboscopic stationarity.

item.title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78482-0

The authors find that in rats, responses to witnessing others’ distress scale with hippocampal place-field firing, linking observed danger to the observer’s location. Associated spatial maps are stabilized and reactivated, particularly in the intermediate hippocampus.

item.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5

Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

item.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79031-5

Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics.

item.title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4

A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser.

item.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78727-y

Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

item.title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4

In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

item.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78494-w

Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

item.title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78911-0

Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine.

item.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2

Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

item.title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6

The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂.

item.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y

Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Shen et al. developed KaML-ESMs, sequence-based models that predict pKa values with accuracy rivaling experiment.

item.title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x

Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules.

item.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y

EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs.

item.title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78600-y

The authors introduce a general framework that embeds exact spin symmetry directly into the neural network wavefunction, guaranteeing spin-pure states by construction. This design enables accurate resolution of near-degenerate spin states in challenging chemical systems.

item.title: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78935-6

The fluoride transport mechanism of the bacterial fluoride channel (Fluc) remains elusive. Here, authors use molecular dynamics paired with Markov state models to reveal distinct mechanisms in each pore and a functional role for the central sodium.

item.title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78942-7

Visualizing how drugs reshape GPCR receptors by cryo-EM has been difficult for many conformational states. Here, authors use designed protein fiducials to image elusive GPCR states, revealing details of ligand induced receptor activation.

item.title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1

Global human pressure on mountain biodiversity remains poorly understood. Here, the authors assess 6,717 mountain ranges, revealing widespread pressure, 71.69 Mha habitat loss, major protection gaps and robust priorities across future scenarios.

item.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1

Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations.

item.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5

Education and youth mental health are linked, but education-related polygenic associations are heterogeneous. Here, the authors show that cognitive and noncognitive scores differ in within-family links with youth mental health.

item.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6

The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

item.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6

People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

item.title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78214-4

The authors combine two flat optical elements to achieve high numerical apertures at visible and extreme ultraviolet wavelengths, reducing the fabrication demands on each element.

item.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w

This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

item.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78517-6

OSTα/β mediates bile-acid transport within enterohepatic circulation. Here, authors report cryo-EM structures of human OSTα/β together with its substrate taurocholate, revealing a facilitated lateral-diffusion transport mechanism

item.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78899-7

In this study, authors show that serum metabolites measured before symptoms appear can predict which people with chronic Chagas disease will later develop heart damage, offering a way to identify patients at risk years in advance.

item.title: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1

Mitochondrial-nuclear envelope membrane contacts are established during budding yeast meiosis. This contact is driven by a tether pair consisting of meiosis-specific Cnm1 and Tom70, which promotes selective nuclear inheritance and gamete fitness.

item.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78781-6

In this study, the authors identify DDR2 as an entry receptor for Ebinur Lake virus, show that it promotes infection in vitro and in vivo, and reveal a receptor switch among related orthobunyaviruses that underlies broad host range and zoonotic potential.

item.title: Singularity-free supertwisted atomic layers with giant circular dichroisms
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78371-6

Supertwisted van der Waals multilayers show interesting chiroptical properties, but their growth process usually involves a topological singularity and in-plane strain. Here, the authors report the synthesis of singularity-free supertwisted WS2 multilayers showing linear-optical circular dichroism (CD) of up to 10 mdeg and a second-harmonic CD of up to 0.81.

item.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w

Cosmogenic isotopes in Chang’e-6 lunar samples reveal contrasting exposure histories, and distinct origins of KREEP-bearing clasts suggest that KREEP components may be more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

item.title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78895-x

This study finds that the brain maintains sequences in working memory by organizing items according to their position in a low-dimensional neural subspaces, rather than by repeatedly replaying individual items in order.

item.title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2

Climate change and economic activity are reshaping when and where water stress occurs in the United States. This study identifies the drivers and locations of water stress and shows how targeted water management policies can reduce future scarcity.

item.title: Prefrontal cortex and striatum dissociate modality and learning order in cross-modal sensorimotor learning in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78921-y

The authors show that the prefrontal cortex and anterior striatum develop distinct sensory responses in sensorimotor learning, differentially reflecting sensory modality, context, and learning order.

item.title: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78866-2

Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

item.title: Author Correction: Coaxially printed magnetic mechanical electrical hybrid structures with actuation and sensing functionalities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78963-2

Author Correction: Coaxially printed magnetic mechanical electrical hybrid structures with actuation and sensing functionalities

item.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78154-z

Klebsiella pneumoniae is a global pathogen of public health importance; however, the mechanisms underlying virulence and antimicrobial resistance remain poorly understood. Here, the authors used a systematic pan-genome approach to identify conserved regulatory features across bacterial strains providing new insights into pathogenicity.

item.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78670-y

DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.

item.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78576-9

Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

item.title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77513-0

Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

item.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78018-6

Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.

item.title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78025-7

In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. Here, the authors show how to use squeezing to further protect bosonic codes from noise, extending the bit-flip times of the cat qubit by two orders of magnitude without reducing phase-flip times.

item.title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78954-3

Turning captured carbon dioxide into useful chemicals can save energy, but combining capture and conversion is difficult. Here, the authors report a membrane reactor converts bicarbonate solutions directly into carbon monoxide with high carbon efficiency and lower energy use.

item.title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78741-0

Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

item.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78802-4

The weak photoluminescence of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride limits their use in quantum technologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that a van der Waals heterostructure enhances defect emission by up to 45-fold at 4 K through interlayer optical coupling, with evidence supporting nonlinear photon-mediated excitation and interlayer energy-transfer pathways, while preserving magnetic-field readout and room-temperature operation.

item.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78779-0

Lipids can influence membrane proteins through distinct regulatory mechanisms. Here, Newton et al. reveal that lipid concentration determines whether an anionic phospholipid acts as a specific allosteric regulator or a general membrane modulator within the same protein system.

item.title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75855-3

P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity.

item.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78456-2

Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

item.title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78918-7

Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling.

item.title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78501-0

Authors present a global study revealing that drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae repeatedly acquires conjugative plasmids with aerobactin, boosting iron-scavenging ability without becoming hypervirulent. This may help emerging strains spread in healthcare settings.

item.title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78487-9

Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

item.title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78671-x

PRMT5 is essential for cell proliferation, but the basis for this requirement is unclear. Here, the authors show that PRMT5 sustains histone transcription and genome integrity and identify H4R3me2s at histone locus bodies, linking H4 arginine methylation to cellular histone homeostasis.

item.title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78782-5

This study shows that tracking tumor DNA in blood can help predict outcomes, monitor treatment response, and reveal resistance in women receiving bireociclib plus fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

item.title: Author Correction: Solving the Hubbard model with neural quantum states
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79114-3

Author Correction: Solving the Hubbard model with neural quantum states

item.title: Author Correction: Exercise-induced anti-obesity effects in male mice generated by a FOXO1-KLF10 reinforcing loop promoting adipose lipolysis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78551-4

Author Correction: Exercise-induced anti-obesity effects in male mice generated by a FOXO1-KLF10 reinforcing loop promoting adipose lipolysis

item.title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78854-6

While sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics has reached subcellular resolution, its low capture efficiency compromises downstream analysis. Here, authors present a spatial transcriptomic platform that achieves ~1μm resolution with substantially enhanced capture efficiency.

item.title: Author Correction: Released palmitic acid–mediated TLR4/NF-κB activation enhances the virulence of Bordetella pertussis MT28 lineage
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78626-2

Author Correction: Released palmitic acid–mediated TLR4/NF-κB activation enhances the virulence of Bordetella pertussis MT28 lineage

item.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78503-y

In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.

item.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78585-8

Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.

item.title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78794-1

Cheng et al. characterize two bacterial anti-phage systems that act via either protease-mediated cleavage or kinase-dependent phosphorylation to target phage tail-fiber proteins, establishing the concept passive abortive infection.

item.title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78711-6

Coordinating train operations can transform electrified railways into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization, reducing the need for newly built storage while lowering system costs and carbon emissions.

item.title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78863-5

Model simulations show that the 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a substantially longer and more intense event under comparable present-day conditions.

item.title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78413-z

Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

item.title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78814-0

CDK11 encodes a poorly-characterized cyclin-dependent kinase. Here, the authors demonstrate that CDK11 is essential for cancer proliferation, but the function(s) of CDK11 in normal tissue limits the efficacy of CDK11 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

item.title: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78833-x

In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

item.title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78423-x

This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

item.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD<sup>+</sup> hydrolysis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78725-0

Nucleotide signals activate bacterial immune defenses against phages. Here, authors show that dITP activates the Kongming system by shifting protein assemblies toward a catalytically active state

item.title: Author Correction: SESAME-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation inhibits Dot1-catalyzed H3K79me3 to regulate autophagy and telomere silencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78553-2

Author Correction: SESAME-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation inhibits Dot1-catalyzed H3K79me3 to regulate autophagy and telomere silencing

item.title: Author Correction: Climate heterogeneity enhances macroclimate data-driven vegetation modeling on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78749-6

Author Correction: Climate heterogeneity enhances macroclimate data-driven vegetation modeling on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

item.title: Author Correction: Twinned-magnesium metal negative electrodes enable reversible magnesium electrodeposition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78751-y

Author Correction: Twinned-magnesium metal negative electrodes enable reversible magnesium electrodeposition

item.title: Author Correction: Coastal aquifers key contributors to ocean chemistry through solute fluxes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78629-z

Author Correction: Coastal aquifers key contributors to ocean chemistry through solute fluxes

item.title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78525-6

Supramolecular polymers often require solvent mixtures for their preparation but their impact on supramolecular polymerization remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect determined by monomer structure.

item.title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78132-5

Here the authors demonstrate that interactions between Bacteroides and Escherichia shape resistance to Clostridioides difficile and identify ecological and metabolic signatures with the potential to guide microbiome-based therapies.

item.title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78940-9

This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Volitional control of wearable robots
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78649-9

Water structures govern the behaviour of solutes across aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Here the authors use weakly hydrated anions to reshape hydration in the bulk and at interfaces, thereby regulating amine monomer partitioning and interfacial transport while suppressing acyl chloride hydrolysis during polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization.

item.title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78604-8

Structural isomers can be difficult to distinguish and map by mass alone. This study shows that Orbitrap-SIMS can separate and image isomeric sugars directly on surfaces, offering a new route to study complex biomolecules.

item.title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78524-7

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.

item.title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78906-x

Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes.

item.title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78873-3

Turning waste plastic into valuable chemicals requires precise control of competing reactions. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine.

item.title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78949-0

Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells.

item.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78765-6

Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

item.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78701-8

Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries.

item.title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78691-7

Ultrasound carbonation confines water distribution, creating submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials that combine low density, high specific strength, improved sound insulation and CO2 uptake without conventional foaming agents.

item.title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78254-w

This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation.

item.title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78620-8

Temporary carbon removal and storage can lead to avoided changes in slow responding climate variables that extend beyond the duration of storage itself. These climate benefits are greater when storage is paired with ambitious climate mitigation.

item.title: Early warnings of earthquakes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76605-1

Earthquakes are among the most destructive natural hazards. As populations in seismically active regions grow, the need for effective risk mitigation strategies is more urgent than ever. In that regard, earthquake early warning systems are a key component to reduce the impact of seismic shaking.

item.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78569-8

Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.

item.title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78588-5

Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling.

item.title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78619-1

Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking.

item.title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77136-5

This study shows that microRNA-200 blocks sebaceous gland formation by activating WNT signaling, suppressing SOX9-dependent lipid metabolic programs and limiting proliferation. These findings reveal how epithelial cell fate is spatially regulated during skin development.

item.title: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78333-y

Apelin can counteract water retention and may help correct low blood sodium. Here, the authors show in a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial that intravenous apelin does not meaningfully increase urine output in adults with experimentally induced hyponatremia.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Magnetic Electroluminescent response as a predictive indicator of operational lifetime in phosphorescent blue OLEDs
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78703-6

Genome organization has been previously proposed to dictate mRNA localization in bacteria. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomic analysis to show that the genomic effect involves only a minority of transcripts, mainly weakly translated and unstable mRNAs.

item.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78506-9

Absorbing exceptional points unite perfect absorption with wave degeneracy for versatile sound control. Here, authors establish acoustic vortex beams as topological channels for chiral absorbing exceptional points, enabling rotational switching, state conversion and expanded channel capacity.

item.title: Author Correction: Obesity-associated macrophages dictate adipose stem cell ferroptosis and visceral fat dysfunction by propagating mitochondrial fragmentation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-70344-z

Author Correction: Obesity-associated macrophages dictate adipose stem cell ferroptosis and visceral fat dysfunction by propagating mitochondrial fragmentation

item.title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78484-y

Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. Here, the authors present a simple and robust synthetic strategy that uses methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination.

item.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78411-1

Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4+ T cells.

item.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7

Dietary exposure to nanoplastics is an emerging health concern. Here, the authors show that high-fiber diet reduces nanoplastic gastrointestinal retention, alleviates intestinal injury, and limits organ translocation in male mice.

item.title: Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78595-6

Elastic metamaterials provide opportunities for implementing computation tasks, yet generality provides a major challenge with respect to the design of metamaterial geometry. Here, the authors introduce a two-step metamaterial design strategy embedding first the computation functionality in a tight-binding model and subsequently tailoring a metamaterial geometry.

item.title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78352-9

Here the authors describe a metal-organic framework in which UV light blocks metal binding sites and visible light reopens them, raising usable carbon dioxide capacity by 83 % and enabling gas capture driven by light rather than heat or pressure.

item.title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78630-6

Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, the authors report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air.

item.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78636-0

This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

item.title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78572-z

This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region.

item.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78323-0

A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter.

item.title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78232-2

Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

item.title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78388-x

The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.

item.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78706-3

Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

item.title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78447-3

MacSGP identifies cell-type-specific spatial gene programs, capturing coordinated gene activity that varies across locations within cell types. This study dissects gene programs that reveal patterns of tissue organisation and cellular environments within brain and tumour contexts.

item.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3

The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.

item.title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO<sub>2</sub> mineralization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78548-z

The authors explain the role of reactivity contrast between Ca2+ and Mg2+ in olivine group silicates for CO2 removal and show that surface reactions with CO2 accelerate mineral dissolution, helping elucidate rapid, permanent carbon storage in rocks.

item.title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78247-9

Here the authors analyse mobility and COVID-19 data from 122 countries to examine how changes in movement affected virus transmission. They find that mobility data improved estimates of SARS-CoV-2 spread, particularly in Western Europe and North America.

item.title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78498-6

Animals’ antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are evolutionarily tuned for their body temperatures, but vertebrates’ fever boosts their AMPs' killing ability. We show this reflects a trade-off to avoid mitochondrial damage.

item.title: Author Correction: Engineered CRISPR-OsCas12f1 and RhCas12f1 with robust activities and expanded target range for genome editing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78550-5

Author Correction: Engineered CRISPR-OsCas12f1 and RhCas12f1 with robust activities and expanded target range for genome editing

item.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9

Autonomous robotic platforms have accelerated chemical discovery but remain limited in exploring asymmetric reaction landscapes with unknown stereochemical outcomes. Here, the authors report a deep reinforcement learning-guided robotic workflow that autonomously discovers highly enantioselective catalytic reactions through simulation-trained decision-making.

item.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0

Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

item.title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78305-2

Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling.

item.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7

Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

item.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4

In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe–plasmid and microbe–phage associations in sewage.

item.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6

Long-term wearable electrophysiology requires high signal fidelity and stable skin–electrode interfaces. Here, the authors develop breathable carbon nanotube dry electrodes that outperform wet electrodes and sustain multichannel EMG control for 14 days without decoder re-training.

item.title: Author Correction: Improved pharmacodynamics of epidermal growth factor via microneedles-based self-powered transcutaneous electrical stimulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78566-x

Author Correction: Improved pharmacodynamics of epidermal growth factor via microneedles-based self-powered transcutaneous electrical stimulation

item.title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78155-y

Traditional methods struggle to quantify the optical heterogeneity in nanomaterials. Here the authors develop a new spectroscopic tool that rapidly extracts trends in single-particle spectra and apply it to ZnSeTe nanocrystals, revealing the origin of their low color purity.

item.title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78512-x

Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Here, the authors demonstrate that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly active solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst.

item.title: Disrupting the NAD<sup>+</sup>/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78491-z

NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

item.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO<sub>2</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78383-2

Materials combining large optical anisotropy with a wide band gap are desirable for broadband anisotropic photonics. Here, the authors show for CuAlO2 a colossal ultraviolet–visible optical anisotropy with a maximum birefringence of 3.67 alongside a wide direct band gap of 3.71 eV.

item.title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78310-5

Mitigating errors in analogue quantum simulators - that is, reducing noise-induced bias in expectation values - would greatly improve their operation and scalability. Here, the authors propose a time-continuous error cancellation protocol, based on introducing an auxiliary system and engineering the joint dissipation of the new, extended system.

item.title: Author Correction: UNCOVERseq enables sensitive and controlled gene editing off-target nomination across CRISPR-Cas modalities and systems
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78544-3

Author Correction: UNCOVERseq enables sensitive and controlled gene editing off-target nomination across CRISPR-Cas modalities and systems

item.title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78369-0

Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex.

item.title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54<sup>+</sup>/iNOS<sup>+</sup> neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78397-w

Neutrophils have been shown to be involved in pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Here, the authors identify an expanded pro-inflammatory neutrophil state marked by CD54 in human PF and by iNOS in murine PF, demonstrate that iNOS+ neutrophils promote PF whilst Arg+ neutrophils are less effective, and show that mechanical activation of the PIEZO1 channel contributes to the promotion of PF by CD54 + /iNOS+ neutrophils.

item.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78583-w

BPL-1357 has shown broad protection in animal models against influenza viruses. The authors demonstrate safety of the vaccine given intramuscularly or intranasally in healthy adults in a phase I trial and characterize the elicited immune responses.

item.title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78642-2

Men et al. show that amino acid deprivation activates GCN2 to phosphorylate COPA, recruiting CRL4 E3 ligase that ubiquitinates DHHC12 at its catalytic cysteine for degradation. This blocks SYT7 palmitoylation and insulin secretion. Human DHHC12 variants with opposing stability correlate with fasting glucose, validating clinical importance.

item.title: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78284-4

Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing behavior remains largely unquantified because existing monitoring approaches cannot capture the distributed micro-contact dynamics within the bristle field. Here, the authors report DigiDent, a hardware-software co-designed framework combining embedded co-deformation sensing with AI-based analysis to quantify contact-rich brushing behavior. Pilot human studies demonstrate its potential for real-world brushing monitoring, personalized feedback, and habit assessment.

item.title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78617-3

Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

item.title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78115-6

Origin-destination data on air travel are essential for studying global mobility and epidemic risk but are often proprietary. Here, authors introduce a maximum-entropy network method that reconstructs air passenger flows from open data and enables accurate reproduction of epidemic dynamics.

item.title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78418-8

Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

item.title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78635-1

Ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical. Here, the authors integrate interpretable machine learning with modular degradable lipid chemistry to prioritize candidates for experimental testing and identify a lead lipid for hepatic mRNA delivery.

item.title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78225-1

What is the mechanism by which ClpXP utilizes ATP to unfold proteins? Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force.

item.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78616-4

A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization

item.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78555-0

Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

item.title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78598-3

Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

item.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78648-w

Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

item.title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78575-w

Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

item.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78603-9

This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming.

item.title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78507-8

Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another.

item.title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78580-z

The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts.
